li_caption:
An S corp is not about how much you sell. It is about how much profit is left.

Four things we check before an owner switches for 2027:

1. Profit. Sole owners and single-member LLCs pay self-employment tax of up to 15.3%, figured on 92.35% of net profit. That is the tax an S corp can reduce.
2. Salary. S corp owners who work in the business must be paid a reasonable wage through payroll before taking distributions. Only the profit above that salary avoids payroll taxes.
3. Costs. Payroll, a separate business return (Form 1120-S) and cleaner books all cost money. If the tax saved doesn't beat them, stay as you are for now.
4. Timing. For a calendar-year business to be an S corp for 2027, Form 2553 is due by March 15, 2027. It can also be filed any time before then. State rules vary, so check yours as well.
